source.author: ov
source.text: Illa nocens spargit virus sucosque veneni et Noctem noctisque deos Ereboque chaoque convocat et longis Hecaten ululatibus orat: exsiluere loco dictu mirabile silvae, ingemuitque solum, vicinaque palluit arbor, sparsaque sanguineis maduerunt pabula guttis, et lapides visi mugitus edere raucos, et latrare canes et humus serpentibus atris squalere et tenues animae volitare videntur.
source.text_original: Illa nocens spargit virus sucosque veneni / et Noctem noctisque deos Ereboque chaoque / convocat et longis Hecaten ululatibus orat: / exsiluere loco (dictu mirabile) silvae, / ingemuitque solum, vicinaque palluit arbor, / sparsaque sanguineis maduerunt pabula guttis, / et lapides visi mugitus edere raucos, / et latrare canes et humus serpentibus atris / squalere et tenues animae volitare videntur.
source.text_english: That wicked woman scatters poison and juices of venom, and calls on Night and the gods of Night and Erebus and Chaos, and prays to Hecate with long howlings. The woods leaped from their place, marvellous to tell, and the ground groaned, and the neighboring tree grew pale, and the pasture grasses, sprinkled with blood-red drops, were wet; and the stones seemed to utter hoarse lowing sounds, and dogs to bark, and the earth to bristle with black snakes, and thin shades to be seen flitting about.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus:
reuse.text_original: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus / extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque / talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus: /
reuse.text_english: and now Cretheus had lifted his faint face to the song, and, looking with sorrow upon both son and daughter-in-law, was opening his lips to say such things, with his blood already poured out:
